How NAVI OS works
A deliberate loop: connect, authorize, consider, approve. You decide what the assistant can see and when it can act.

<svg class="method__svg" viewbox="0 0 400 400"><circle class="method__track" cx="200" cy="200" r="170"></circle><circle class="method__arc" cx="200" cy="200" pathlength="1" r="170" stroke-dasharray="1 1" stroke-dashoffset="0"></circle></svg>

• Connect the extension

    Build and load the unpacked Chrome extension, configure its ID, and connect the localhost backend from the popup.

• Grant browser permissions

    Enroll the tabs you choose. Allow visible text separately when you want page analysis.

• Receive contextual suggestions

    Analyze one or two authorized pages, or opt into Ghost Mode for supported metadata patterns.

• Review and approve actions

    Choose suggested queries, enable search-opening permission, and explicitly approve. Only selected Google search tabs open.

Private by permission

• NAVI OS / PRIVACY & CONTROL

    Explicit access

    Only enrolled tabs participate. Page text needs separate consent and an explicit extraction request. Navigation invalidates content permission.

• NAVI OS / PRIVACY & CONTROL

    Your session, your choice

    Ghost Mode is off by default. Monitoring uses enrolled metadata, with session-only aggregate counters. Pause, disable, or erase it in the popup.

• NAVI OS / PRIVACY & CONTROL

    Approval before action

    Suggestions never open pages on their own. Search opening needs a separate permission, selected queries, and explicit approval.

• NAVI OS / PRIVACY & CONTROL

    Transparency within reach

    Inspect enrolled tabs, consent, pattern counters, and pending suggestions in the popup. Persistent interaction history and general browser automation are not implemented.
Good questions

What does NAVI OS do?

NAVI OS combines deterministic browser intelligence with optional server-side Gemini planning and summaries. Gemini receives captured context only after consent. Unsupported or unavailable model responses fall back safely.

How do permissions work?

Metadata enrollment, visible text, Ghost monitoring, localhost transfer, and search opening are separate opt-ins. Manage and revoke them in the extension popup.

What does Ghost Mode mean?

Optional monitoring of enrolled tab metadata to detect supported development patterns. It does not read page text or automatically upload browsing activity.

Which capabilities are available today?

Authorized context, ContextFlow, and opt-in Ghost suggestions work in the extension. The paired dashboard adds Gemini plans and approved search, origin opening, switching, and same-window grouping. General automation, persistent history, and Supabase are not implemented.

Can I control everything from the website?

The dashboard checks connectivity and offers an assistant through a separate session pairing grant issued in the extension popup. It can read enrolled context and execute selected approved actions. Permissions and Ghost Mode remain controlled in the popup.
